threads.body:
`freepdb1` is the PDB/service name, but semconv defines Oracle `db.namespace` as `DB_UNIQUE_NAME` (`FREE` in this image). The other contracts expect the semconv value (e.g. PostgreSQL's `conformance|conformance`), so this bakes Java's current behavior into a cross-language contract. Same for the other three scenarios. Maybe expect the semconv value and track the Java gap (the PDB name fits `oracle.db.pdb` / `oracle.db.service`)?

```suggestion
              db.namespace: FREE
```

threads.body: Nit, non-blocking: is `{call …}` meant to exercise the JDBC escape-syntax handling? It's fine while only Java runs this contract. But the contract describes itself as shared by every language, and other Oracle drivers (python-oracledb, node-oracledb) don't accept escape syntax. If the native form is fine, `CALL conformance.noop()` would match the MariaDB and PostgreSQL contracts. If the escape syntax is intended, a short comment saying so would help whoever adds the next language.
